claims.text: The initial Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni eutectic alloy has a continuous, brittle dual-phase lamellar microstructure that exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking and low room-temperature ductility.
Severe plastic deformation at 0.4–0.5 Tm followed by rapid quenching will transform the continuous lamellar structure into a patterned or equiaxed nanolamellar structure.
The transformed structure will contain high-angle grain boundaries and have a reduced interfacial coherence length.
The proposed treatment will preserve the bulk Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni composition.
A temperature window of 0.4–0.5 Tm, estimated as 600–800 °C, is required for successful treatment.
Deformation pressure above 5 GPa is required for successful treatment.
High-intensity deformation introduces a high density of dislocations and shear bands that disrupt continuous lamellae.
At 0.4–0.5 Tm, dynamic recovery and recrystallization will break up brittle interfaces.
The proposed intermediate-temperature treatment will avoid excessive grain coarsening and phase decomposition.
Heusler-phase formation or persistence is a processing concern in compositionally related Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti alloys containing Hf or Mo.
Heusler phases in these alloys are brittle and mechanically detrimental.
The patterned structure will redistribute interfacial stress concentrations and prevent crack propagation along continuous interfaces.
Disruption of continuous interfaces will enable uniform plastic flow.
The treatment will significantly increase room-temperature ductility and fracture toughness.
The refined patterned microstructure will maintain high strength and break the strength-ductility trade-off.
Conventional HIP or standard annealing typically causes grain coarsening or retention of the continuous lamellar structure.
Conventional thermal treatments can retain unwanted Heusler phases in related Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti-Hf alloys.
Temperatures above 0.6 Tm may dissolve or reduce strengthening phases.
Temperatures above 0.6 Tm may produce unwanted Heusler phases.
Temperatures below 0.3 Tm will provide insufficient recovery to break lamellar continuity and may cause brittle fracture during deformation.
